=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s update is not a balanced package for Wattlebridge. It shifts ordinary transaction risk to the Buyer while the Disclosure Letter makes clear that several important matters remain unresolved. The general data-room disclosure and broad limits on claims are particularly problematic: they could undermine specific warranties, remedies and the value of targeted protections.

### Key points to push back on

**1. Liability cap, thresholds and claim period**

- **General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m):** This may be inadequate for material warranty breaches. Seek a higher cap, supported by the diligence and risk profile, and ensure it does not apply to fraud, deliberate concealment, title or capacity, tax, specific indemnities, or other expressly protected claims.
- **De minimis and tipping basket:** The AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket reduce recovery for numerous smaller losses. Seek a lower or no de minimis and a **tipping basket** (once crossed, recover from the first dollar), or negotiate thresholds that exclude specified claims.
- **18-month warranty period:** Too short for issues that may emerge after integration or through audits, particularly tax, title and specific indemnity matters. Seek longer periods and distinct survival periods for tax and fundamental warranties, with claims preserved if notified before expiry and pursued under agreed procedures.
- **“All Claims” time limit:** Reject applying warranty deadlines across all claims by default. Different claims need tailored periods; no contractual time bar should truncate fraud or deliberate concealment claims.

**2. Fundamental warranties and limitations**

The Seller proposes putting capacity and title under the same cap and time limits as general warranties. Reject that. The Seller should give robust, appropriately uncapped or separately capped fundamental warranties on its capacity to sell and its title to the shares, with longer survival. DD-012 is evidence of what the register records, not a substitute for warranties that the Seller owns and can transfer the full 100% interest free of encumbrances.

**3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance**

The proposed application of limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to *all* claims is overbroad. Preserve the Buyer’s rights for fraud, deliberate concealment, specific indemnities and other negotiated carve-outs; do not allow an exclusive-remedy clause to displace remedies for those matters. Non-reliance language should not negate express contractual warranties or claims for misleading conduct or fraud. Have counsel check enforceability and interaction with the final SPA under NSW law.

**4. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge**

- **General data-room disclosure:** Reject disclosure of every fact in a large data room and public registers as sufficient to qualify warranties. It creates uncertainty about what was disclosed and makes it harder to identify which warranty is affected. Require specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter. Preserve the specific disclosures without treating the entire data room as a blanket qualification.
- **Knowledge bar:** Reject a bar for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered. It can turn diligence into a waiver of contractual protection and make “discoverable” an uncertain standard. At most, limit the bar to actual, documented knowledge of named senior Buyer personnel, with no imputation from advisers or constructive knowledge, and retain claims for fraud and deliberate concealment.

**5. Bluefen consent and conditions**

Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue, and the draft disclosure says there is no final written consent or evidence the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. “Reasonable endeavours” and deeming the condition satisfied on delivery of a consent are insufficient if conditions remain outstanding. Require, as a condition precedent to Completion, final written consent **and** evidence that all associated conditions have been met or waived. If not obtained, the Buyer should have a termination right or another agreed protection—not be deemed satisfied.

**6. Riverlark facility and debt-free/cash-free mechanics**

The approximately AUD 3.2m facility remains outstanding, with no repayment or final security discharge in the data room. A release only after Completion exposes the Buyer and Company to continuing debt and security risk, inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline. Require repayment and discharge at or before Completion, lender releases, and an effective funds-flow mechanism that pays the lender directly from sale proceeds if necessary. Include a specific indemnity for any residual facility, security or related liability.

**7. Completion funds flow and bonuses**

The AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from the draft funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. Require the bonuses and all associated costs to be expressly allocated and accounted for in the price mechanics and funds flow. Clarify whether they are debt-like items, transaction expenses or another agreed adjustment; avoid leaving the Company or Buyer to bear undisclosed pre-Completion costs. Seek supporting payroll calculations and a specific protection for any unpaid amounts and on-costs.

**8. Ironquay IP**

The disclosed contract makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but is not independent proof of non-payment, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. Limiting the indemnity to the SOW3 payment is not enough: payment alone may not establish that all relevant IP was effectively transferred. Require verified payment and a signed assignment (or other effective transfer confirmation) before Completion, together with warranties on ownership, chain of title and freedom from encumbrances. Retain a specific indemnity for any loss, liability or remediation relating to the matter.

**9. Export/privacy incident**

The preliminary DD-006 facts involve a link sent to an unintended external address and potentially 1,240 personal-data records; access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. Calling this “not expected to be material” does not resolve that uncertainty. Require further investigation and delivery of findings before Completion, appropriate remediation and any required notifications, and a specific indemnity for incident-related claims, regulatory costs and remediation. Include a condition or termination right if findings reveal material exposure.

**10. Supplier renewals**

The three renewals total AUD 330,000, but the disclosures do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Do not accept the Seller’s assertion that they are routine operating costs without contract review. Confirm renewal terms, termination rights, accrued amounts and whether any liability falls within the agreed price mechanics; seek a targeted warranty or adjustment where warranted.

**11. Other diligence points**

- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a notification obligation, not a share-sale consent requirement. Confirm the clause and require any required notice to be given; do not assume consent is required or that notice is immaterial.
- **Mossvale:** DD-009 identifies an assignment restriction, but not a consent requirement triggered merely by a share sale. Confirm whether the proposed transaction triggers it and obtain any required consent or waiver if it does.
- **Title:** Verify the register and corporate records independently, but retain express seller warranties as to full legal and beneficial ownership, no encumbrances, and valid transfer of all shares.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. **Reject** blanket data-room/public-register disclosure and the broad Buyer-knowledge bar.
2. **Carve out** title, capacity, tax, fraud/deliberate concealment and specific indemnities from inappropriate caps, baskets, short time limits and exclusive-remedy restrictions; negotiate suitable separate limits where uncapped liability is not agreed.
3. **Make Bluefen consent and its conditions, Riverlark repayment/security discharge, and effective Ironquay IP transfer** completion deliverables or conditions, with workable termination or other remedies if not achieved.
4. **Reconcile the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs** expressly in the completion accounts/funds flow and protect the Buyer against unpaid pre-Completion amounts.
5. **Obtain an incident investigation and targeted privacy indemnity**, and verify the supplier renewals and any lease or Mossvale transaction-triggered obligations.
6. Have the final SPA’s claim, disclosure, remedy and limitation provisions reviewed together under NSW law; the commercial effect depends on their interaction, not the Seller’s summary alone.
